correctness.rationale: In A=kQ/J², vertex idempotents and corner arrow spaces E_ab give the full two-sided ideal normal form I(S,U), where selecting vertex S forces every incident arrow subspace; proof works with loops and in characteristic two (a representative e+ell, with ell²=0, yields e via its quadratic identity). For two such ideals IK=0 iff selected supports S,T are disjoint and, blockwise, a in S forces V_ab=0 while b in T forces U_ab=0. Enumerating 0/L/R vertex states gives the nine entries W_m with F_m(T)=sum_d Gaussian(m,d)_q T^d, including the forbidden L-to-R edge. Independence of corner blocks yields the all-quiver bivariate polynomial with vertex weights. Independently evaluated all 3^3 colorings on a source fork and its reversal over q=2,3, obtaining total 69 and coefficients fork [X^4Y^3]=1, [X^3Y^4]=0, reversed coefficient 0; two parallel arrows yield q²+8q+20 (40 and 53 for q=2,3). These finite tests support but do not replace the all-quiver ideal algebra argument. For an empty quiver one can interpret the zero algebra and the empty product as 1; the ordinary unital algebra convention generally assumes at least one vertex.
residual_risks: Finite computational checks q=2,3 are not a substitute for the all-quiver proof.

originality.rationale: The full earlier all-quiver ideal-Grassmannian theorem gives exactly the same single-ideal normal form and Gaussian ideal dimension polynomial, which are NOT novel here. Its count does not impose an ordered product constraint between distinct ideals, so cannot recover the bivariate IK=0 statistic from marginal ideal polynomials. Another earlier all-arity zero-product theorem counts algebra ELEMENT tuples rather than ordered IDEAL pairs; a cycle-graph theorem likewise counts elements. Catoiu–Chin–Krop ideal-semigroup framework is conceptually broad but its inspected full manuscript lacks this exact all-quiver Gaussian three-state pair-count theorem. The new orientation-sensitive double-dimension result survives best-of-knowledge originality, with risk of unindexed stronger ideal-semigroup results.

The polynomial refines edge counts by both ideal dimensions for every finite quiver with loops and multiple arrows and any prime-power field; the smallest fork distinguishes arrow orientation even when single-ideal dimension counts are identical. This reusable exact structural classification and orientation obstruction is mathematically motivated, not a known-table recomputation or trivial isolated instance.
